description: Validate a number written in scientific notation. The number may start with an optional minus sign, followed by a mantissa that is either an integer or a decimal with exactly one digit before and at least one digit after the decimal point. The mantissa must be followed by 'e' or 'E', an optional plus or minus sign, and one or more digits for the exponent. No spaces or other characters allowed.

intent: signed decimal number with an optional fractional part
description: Rule 1: The number may be prefixed with an optional '+' or '-'. Rule 2: The integer part must be one or more digits. Rule 3: If a decimal point is present, it must be followed by one or more digits. Rule 4: No leading zeros are allowed in the integer part unless the integer part is exactly '0'. Rule 5: No spaces or thousands separators are allowed.

intent: signed decimal number with an optional fractional part
description: The string must match a decimal number with the following constraints: it starts with an optional minus sign; then there is at least one digit before the decimal point; if a decimal point appears, it must be followed by exactly two digits; the number must not have leading zeros unless it is zero; no other characters are allowed.

intent: euro price in French format (comma decimal, space thousands, trailing €)
description: A price in euros using French formatting: digits may be grouped by spaces in threes, the decimal separator is a comma, and the euro sign follows the number with no space.

intent: US dollar amount with optional cents
description: A US dollar amount. The number must start with a dollar sign, followed by digits; cents are optional and, if present, must be exactly two digits after a dot. The integer part may include commas as thousands separators, but only if they are correctly placed every three digits.

For our internal accounting export, we need to validate strings that represent prices. A price is written with digits, an optional euro sign at the beginning, and exactly two decimal places separated by a dot. The integer part must not have a leading zero unless the value is between zero and one, in which case a single zero is required before the dot.

Our appointment booking widget has a free-text time field, and customers keep typing whatever they want. We only accept a clock time on the 12-hour scale: an hour from 1 to 12, then a colon, then exactly two digits from 00 to 59 for the minutes, and finally either AM or PM. The AM/PM part may be written in any mix of upper and lower case, and a single space before it is allowed but not required.

Validate an abbreviated English month name for a billing-period dropdown.
Constraints:
1. Accept exactly the three-letter abbreviation of a Gregorian month: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, or Dec.
2. Matching is case-insensitive.
3. No other abbreviation is accepted, including Sept for September and the two-letter forms.
4. No surrounding whitespace and no trailing punctuation (a following period is invalid).

Match a time of day on the 24-hour clock: two digits for the hour from 00 through 23, a colon, and two digits for the minutes from 00 through 59. The seconds may optionally follow as another colon and two digits from 00 through 59.

Validate a three-letter month abbreviation for a reporting filter.
Requirements:
1. The value must be exactly one of the twelve English month abbreviations: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec.
2. Letters may be in any case combination.
3. The value must be exactly three letters; abbreviations such as Sept, the full month name, or a single letter are rejected.
4. A trailing period is not allowed.

We generate sortable IDs for events and need to confirm a submitted ID is a well-formed ULID: twenty-six characters in total. The first ten characters are Crockford's base32 timestamp encoding, each being a digit 0-9 or an uppercase letter except I, L, O and U. The remaining sixteen characters use the same alphabet. Case is not normalized for us, so lowercase input must also be accepted, and the string must be exactly the identifier with no extra characters.

Validate that a string is a version 4 UUID in canonical RFC 4122 form:
- Five groups of hexadecimal digits separated by hyphens, with sizes 8, 4, 4, 4 and 12.
- The first character of the third group must be 4.
- The first character of the fourth group must be one of 8, 9, A, B, a or b.
- Hexadecimal digits may be uppercase or lowercase.
- No characters before or after the UUID are allowed.

A CSS length value as a string: an optional sign (+ or -), one or more decimal digits, an optional fractional part consisting of a dot and one or more digits, followed by a unit. The unit must be one of the following, case-insensitively: px, em, rem, vw, vh, cm, mm, in, pt, pc. No whitespace is allowed anywhere.

Match a URL that starts with either http:// or https:// (case-insensitive). It must contain a host that consists of one or more labels separated by dots, where each label is one or more alphanumeric characters or hyphens (but cannot start or end with a hyphen). The host must end with a dot and a top-level domain of at least two letters. The host may be followed by an optional port number (one or more digits) and an optional path, query string, and fragment. The entire string must be a valid URL according to this description.

Validate an IPv4 address in dotted-quad notation. Rules:
1. Exactly four decimal octets separated by single dots.
2. Each octet is written without leading zeros unless the octet is exactly "0".
3. Each octet's numeric value is between 0 and 255 inclusive.
4. No other characters are permitted, and the whole string must be the address (no surrounding whitespace).

Our admin dashboard has a server field where operators type in the IP address of a machine. We need to reject anything that is not a plain IPv4 address: four numbers separated by dots, each number between 0 and 255, no leading zeros on numbers other than zero itself, and nothing else in the field.
tcp/udp port 1-65535 no leading zeros

intent: username that cannot start or end with a separator
description: We need to let users pick a handle for their public profile page. The handle can contain lowercase letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens, must be between 3 and 30 characters long, and cannot begin or end with a dot, underscore or hyphen.

intent: email address from a specific domain
description: Match an email address that belongs to the example.com domain. The local part may contain letters, digits, dots, underscores, plus signs or hyphens and must start with a letter or digit and end with a letter or digit. The domain must be exactly example.com, case-insensitive.
french mobile number with optional spaces hyphens or dots between digits

Our CRM stores French phone numbers. We need to validate that a number is a valid French landline or mobile number in the national format. It must have exactly 10 digits, starting with 0. The second digit can be 1 through 9 for landlines, or 6 or 7 for mobiles. Spaces, hyphens and dots are allowed as separators but only between digits, and there should be no separator at the very beginning or end.

Match an international phone number in E.164 format. It must start with a plus sign, followed by a non-zero digit, and then up to 14 more digits. The total number of digits after the plus must be between 2 and 15.
our checkout only accepts French postal codes for delivery addresses. A valid code is exactly five digits, and it cannot be all zeros.

Customers in the UK enter their postcode at checkout. Accept the standard UK format: one or two letters for the area, one or two digits for the district, an optional letter, a space, a digit, then two letters for the sector.
For US shipping we need the ZIP code. It can be a five-digit ZIP, or a ZIP+4 with five digits, a hyphen, and four digits. Leading zeros are allowed.
French business registration numbers are either a SIREN (9 digits) or a SIRET (14 digits). We only check the format, not any key.

description: pin code 4 to 6 digits not all the same

description: API key must start with the prefix 'sk_live_' followed by exactly 24 alphanumeric characters (case-sensitive).

intent: passphrase of at least four words
description: A passphrase must consist of at least four words separated by a single space. Each word must contain at least one character and consist only of lowercase letters (a-z).

intent: API key with a known prefix
description: For our internal API, we need to validate secret keys. The format must start with the prefix 'api_' followed by exactly 32 hexadecimal digits (0-9, a-f).

We need to automatically detect our test files in the repo so the CI can run them separately. A file counts as a test file if its name is made of one or more dot-separated parts (no slashes, only letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens in each part), followed by either .spec.ts or .test.js; the part right before that suffix must be exactly 'spec' or 'test', and the whole file name must be at least one character before it, so '.spec.ts' alone doesn't count.

Match a hidden file name that begins with a dot and contains at least one more character; neither "." nor ".." are hidden files, the name cannot contain a slash, and the entire name (including the leading dot) must not be longer than 255 characters.

intent: semantic version with pre-release and build metadata
description: Match a semantic version string with optional pre-release and build metadata. The main version consists of three dot-separated numeric identifiers without leading zeros. Pre-release is a hyphen followed by one or more dot-separated identifiers, each containing only alphanumeric characters and hyphens, and numeric identifiers must not have leading zeros. Build metadata is a plus sign followed by one or more dot-separated identifiers of alphanumeric characters and hyphens.

Our software releases use a year.month version where the year is four digits and the month is two digits from 01 to 12. The release field in our database must accept exactly this format with no leading zeros in the year part.

We require semantic versioning for all our npm packages. A valid version is exactly three dot-separated numeric parts. The major, minor, and patch numbers must not have leading zeros unless the number is zero itself. Pre-release and build metadata are not allowed in this context.

A CSS class name must follow the BEM naming convention: an optional block name in lowercase letters, followed by zero or more element parts each prefixed with a double underscore, followed by zero or more modifier parts each prefixed with a double hyphen. Every part consists of lowercase letters and digits only, must start with a letter, and may contain hyphens between word segments as long as no two hyphens are adjacent. The whole string must be a valid CSS class name according to BEM.

An environment variable name consists of one or more ASCII letters, digits, or underscores, but it must not be empty and must not begin with a digit. Additionally, it must not be a single underscore, and the name must not end with an underscore.

Our configuration files use two naming styles for variables depending on the context. Local variables follow snake_case: lowercase words separated by single underscores. Global constants follow SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE: uppercase words separated by single underscores. A name is either a local variable or a global constant, never a mix of both cases. It must have at least one word, each word must start with a letter, and words may contain digits after the first character.

A kebab-case identifier for our CSS custom properties and HTML attributes must:
- consist of one or more lowercase alphanumeric words separated by single hyphens
- each word must start with a letter
- digits may appear after the first character of a word
- no leading or trailing hyphen, no consecutive hyphens

We need a field for blog post headlines: the author types a headline and we must accept it only if it is written in title case, meaning every word starts with an uppercase letter followed by zero or more lowercase letters, and single spaces separate the words.

Validate a quoted string. Rules:
1. The whole string must be enclosed in a pair of matching quote characters; accepted quote characters are the double quote (") and the single quote (').
2. The content between the quotes must be at least one character long.
3. The content may not contain the quote character that opened the string.
4. The content may not contain a newline character.
5. Only the format is checked; nothing about the meaning of the content is validated.
6. When the opening quote is a double quote, the content may contain single quotes, and vice versa.

description: sentence capital first letter ends with period single spaces no newline
text containing at least one word repeated consecutively with a space between

description: Support is getting complaints that people paste fragments into the 'message' box on the contact form. match: The cat sat on the mat.

description: Validates a personal name. The string must consist of one or more letter characters from any Unicode script, optionally separated by single hyphen or apostrophe characters. Leading and trailing separators are not allowed, and consecutive separators are not allowed.

intent: name in any language with letters, hyphens and apostrophes
description: A name can contain letters from any language, and single hyphens or apostrophes between parts. It must start and end with a letter.

intent: number using any Unicode decimal digits
description: A numeric string that uses only decimal digit characters from any Unicode script. No separators, signs, or whitespace are allowed.

intent: name in any language with letters, hyphens and apostrophes
description: Validates a display name for international users. The name must contain at least one letter from any Unicode script. It may additionally contain hyphens or apostrophes, but only as separators between letters, not at the start or end, and not consecutively.

description: Match a comma-separated list of three to eight integers, each between -999 and 999 inclusive, with no trailing comma.

description:
Validate a file size string. Rules:
1. The value is a non-negative decimal number with at most one decimal point; it may have a fractional part with up to two digits.
2. A space is required between the number and the unit.
3. The unit is one of B, KB, MB, GB, TB, in either uppercase or lowercase, and case must not be mixed within the unit.
4. Leading zeros are not allowed on the integer part unless the integer part is exactly zero.
decimal longitude -180 to 180 optional minus decimals required
Match a positive integer that has no leading zeros. A single zero on its own is not allowed.

Our inventory system assigns each product a shipping quantity code. The code is a plain whole number, always greater than zero, and it must never start with zero because the warehouse scanner trims leading digits and duplicates records. The field may only contain the digits of that quantity, nothing else.

Match a number written in scientific notation: an optional sign, then a significand that is an integer or has a fractional part with a dot and at least one digit after it, then an e or E, an optional sign, and a whole-number exponent of one or more digits.
Accept a positive whole number. Constraints: one or more digits; the first digit must not be zero; no sign, decimal point, whitespace or thousands separators are permitted.

intent: signed decimal number with an optional fractional part
description: Accept a signed decimal. Rules: an optional leading plus or minus sign; then one or more digits; optionally a decimal point followed by one or more digits. A bare sign, a trailing decimal point and a fractional-only value are all invalid.

Our reporting dashboard has a dropdown for the month, and the labels coming from the upstream export sometimes use the three-letter English month abbreviation. We want to validate that field before storing it, accepting only genuine three-letter month abbreviations, in any casing, with an optional trailing period. Anything that looks like a month name but isn't an actual month abbreviation, or that has extra text, should be rejected.

For our shift-planning tool we store the time of day in 24-hour notation. The value must be a two-digit hour from 00 to 23, a two-digit minute from 00 to 59, and, optionally, a two-digit second from 00 to 59 introduced by a colon. Hours, minutes and seconds are all required to be written with two digits, and the value must be the whole field, with no surrounding spaces.

intent: git commit hash, short or full
description: Our deployment dashboard needs to link out to a commit when users paste a hash into the search box. Only full or abbreviated Git commit hashes are accepted: that means 7 to 40 hexadecimal characters, and we treat them as case-insensitive.

intent: product SKU with a fixed pattern of letters and digits
description: The warehouse system generates product SKUs as two uppercase letters, a hyphen, three digits, another hyphen, and a final uppercase letter. We need to validate that a scanned code follows exactly this format before accepting it.

intent: git commit hash, short or full
description: Match a Git commit hash. It can be either the full 40-character hexadecimal form or the abbreviated 7-character form, and hexadecimal digits may be upper or lower case.

Validate a hexadecimal string according to the following rules:
- The string must consist solely of hexadecimal digits (0-9, a-f, A-F).
- It must have an even length, at least 2 characters.
- No other characters, spaces, or separators are allowed.
A ULID is a 26-character string: the first 10 characters are Crockford base32 uppercase letters or digits, and the remaining 16 are the same alphabet.

Validate a CSS hex color code. It must start with a hash symbol. It can be either 3 digits, 4 digits, 6 digits, or 8 digits. Each digit must be a hexadecimal character (0-9, a-f, A-F). The entire string must be exactly the color code with no extra characters.

intent: domain name with a given top-level domain
description: Match a domain name that ends with the top-level domain .org. The domain must consist of one or more labels separated by dots. Each label may contain letters, digits, and hyphens, but must not start or end with a hyphen. The last label must be exactly 'org'. The whole string is the domain.

intent: HTML opening tag of a given element
description: Match an HTML opening tag for a div element. The tag must start with '<div', followed by zero or more attributes. Each attribute must have a name, optionally followed by an equals sign and a value. The value, if present, must be either a double-quoted string (which can contain any character except a double quote) or a single-quoted string (which can contain any character except a single quote). Attribute names must consist of one or more letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores, starting with a letter. Attributes are separated by one or more whitespace characters. The tag ends with '>'. The tag is case-sensitive and must be exactly 'div'.

Our admin dashboard has a field where operators type the address of a device on the local network, so we need to make sure they entered a normal four-part IPv4 address and nothing else. Each of the four parts must be a plain decimal number from 0 to 255, with no leading zeros unless the part is exactly zero, and the parts must be separated by single dots.
Check that a string is a valid IPv4 address in dotted-decimal form. It must have exactly four numeric parts separated by dots, and each part must be between 0 and 255 without leading zeros.
twitter-style handle @ followed by 4-15 letters digits underscores

We are collecting work email addresses on our B2B signup page and want to reject anything that plainly is not an address. Accept letters, digits, dots, underscores and hyphens in the part before the @, with the part before the @ starting with a letter or digit. After the @ there must be at least one dot, the name before the dot must be letters, digits or hyphens starting and ending with a letter or digit, and the ending must be at least two letters (any case).

intent: North American phone number with optional formatting
description: A North American phone number consists of a three-digit area code, a three-digit central office code, and a four-digit line number. The area code and central office code must each begin with a digit from 2 through 9, and the line number may be any four digits. The number may be written as ten consecutive digits, or with any of these separators allowed only in their proper positions: a hyphen or a dot or a space, or parentheses around the area code; parentheses may be accompanied by an optional space or hyphen after the closing parenthesis. Mixed separators are not permitted, so the area code, central office code, and line number must be joined by the same kind of separator throughout, except that parenthesized area codes may use their own trailing separator. The string may optionally begin with a plus sign followed by the digits 1, representing the country code, and that prefix may be followed by a space or a hyphen before the rest of the number.
french phone number, ten digits starting with 0, optional spaces every two digits

Our deployment tool reads the version constraint field that developers type into the manifest. It only accepts a plain exact version or an upper-bound constraint meaning 'compatible up to but not including the next major release', written as a version with a tilde in front of it. A version is a major number, a dot, a minor number, and optionally a dot and a patch number. Leading zeros are not allowed on any number.

A semantic version number consists of three dot-separated non-negative integers with no leading zeros, optionally followed by a pre-release part starting with a hyphen and then one or more dot-separated identifiers, where each identifier is either digits with no leading zeros or an alphanumeric identifier containing at least one letter or hyphen; and optionally followed by a build metadata part starting with a plus sign and then one or more dot-separated identifiers of letters, digits and hyphens. The build metadata may appear even when there is no pre-release part.

Our logistics API accepts a date-only field from partners. It must be a calendar date written in the ISO 8601 extended format: four-digit year, then two-digit month, then two-digit day, separated by hyphens. A leading plus sign on the year is tolerated. Only the format is checked, not whether the month/day combination is a real date.

Validate a date in day/month/year order using slashes as separators. Rules: the day is either a single digit 1-9 or two digits (01-31); the month is either a single digit 1-9 or two digits (01-12); the year is exactly four digits, no sign. Only the format is checked, not calendar validity.

Check that the string is a date in dd/mm/yyyy form: exactly two digits for the day, exactly two digits for the month, and exactly four digits for the year, separated by slashes. Only the format is checked, not calendar validity.

Match a 24-hour clock time. Hours go from 00 to 23 and minutes from 00 to 59, separated by a colon. Seconds, also from 00 to 59, are optional; when present they follow a second colon. Nothing else may appear in the string.
url slug lowercase words separated by single hyphens

tcp/udp port number 1-65535 plain digits no leading zeros

No other characters are allowed.

intent: file name with a date prefix
description: Validate a file name that starts with an ISO 8601 date prefix of the form YYYY-MM-DD (four digits, hyphen, two digits, hyphen, two digits), followed by exactly one underscore, then a slug. The slug must start with a lowercase letter and may contain only lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. The file name must end with a conventional extension: one of .js, .ts, or .json. Month, day, and calendar validity are not checked; only the format is enforced.

intent: file name with a date prefix
description: Validate a file name with a date prefix. description: We need to validate uploaded file names for our document archive. Each uploaded document must carry a date prefix in the form YYYY-MM-DD directly followed by an underscore; the archive software rejects anything else. After the underscore the file name may contain letters, digits, parentheses, spaces, and hyphens, but no other punctuation. The extension must be .pdf (case-insensitive). The date itself is just a format check — we don't care whether the month or day is real.

intent: semantic version with pre-release and build metadata
description:
Validate a semantic version string per the following rules:
- Three dot-separated numeric components: major, minor, patch.
- Each numeric component is either 0 or a positive integer with no leading zero (e.g., 0, 1, 10; not 01).
- May be followed by an optional pre-release section: a hyphen then one or more dot-separated identifiers; each identifier consists of alphanumerics and hyphens, must be non-empty, and if it is purely numeric it must not have a leading zero.
- May be followed by an optional build metadata section: a plus sign then one or more dot-separated identifiers; each identifier consists of alphanumerics and hyphens and must be non-empty.
- If both pre-release and build metadata are present, the pre-release must come first, followed by the build metadata.
- Only the format is checked; no checksums or calendar facts are validated.

Validate a calendar version string in the format YYYY.MM, where YYYY is a four-digit year (no leading zero restriction beyond being four digits overall) and MM is a two-digit month from 01 to 12. A leading zero is required for months 1 through 9. The string must contain exactly one dot separating the year and month, with no extra characters.
title case text: words separated by single spaces, each word starting with an uppercase letter followed by lowercase letters only

intent: sentence starting with a capital letter and ending with a period
description:
A single sentence on one line. Rules:
1. The first character is an uppercase letter.
2. The sentence ends with a period.
3. At most one period exists in the whole string, and it is the final character.
4. The period may not appear in the middle: no other period occurs anywhere.
5. The rest of the sentence may contain letters, digits, spaces, commas, apostrophes and hyphens, but no periods, no line breaks.

intent: name in any language with letters, hyphens and apostrophes
description: Our signup form has a display-name field and we keep getting support tickets from users whose names are rejected. We want to accept any real human name: any language's letters are fine, and names may contain hyphens or apostrophes between letters. Nothing else — no digits, no spaces, no symbols.

intent: name in any language with letters, hyphens and apostrophes
description:
Validate a personal name field according to these rules:
1. The name consists of one or more letters, using the full Unicode letter property (any script, including combining marks used in names).
2. Hyphens and apostrophes may appear, but only between two letters — never at the start or end of the whole name, and never two separators in a row.
3. Both the ASCII apostrophe and the right single quotation mark (U+2019) count as apostrophes.
4. No leading or trailing whitespace and no empty string.
5. Any other character (digits, punctuation, spaces) makes the input invalid.

intent: name in any language with letters, hyphens and apostrophes
description:
Check a surname/last-name field with these constraints:
- Must be non-empty.
- Allowed characters: Unicode letters, and the combining marks that attach to them (so scripts such as Devanagari and Thai are handled).
- A single hyphen or apostrophe may separate two letter parts, e.g. inside compound names. Hyphens and apostrophes must be flanked by letters on both sides and may not appear at either end of the string.
- Only ASCII hyphen-minus counts as a hyphen; only ASCII apostrophe counts as an apostrophe.
- Digits, spaces and all other punctuation are rejected.

intent: name in any language with letters, hyphens and apostrophes
description:
A "given name" field must satisfy:
1. At least one character.
2. Every character is a Unicode letter, a Unicode combining mark (allowed so that names in Indic, Arabic and similar scripts validate), or the ASCII hyphen-minus or ASCII apostrophe.
3. The value may not start or end with a hyphen or apostrophe.
4. Two separators may not be adjacent (no "--", "''" or "-'" sequences).
5. No whitespace, digits or other symbols.

Since the register is sentence, I can write: 'Match a UK mobile number. It is 11 digits long, starts with 07, and may contain spaces after the first five digits and after the next three digits.' But that would allow spaces only in those positions? Or both? Typically, if spaces are used, they are used consistently. So I can say: 'It can be written with or without spaces. If spaces are used, they must be placed after the first five digits and after the next three digits.' That means the number is either 11 digits continuous, or 07XXX XXX XXX (with two spaces). So the pattern: ^(07\d{9}|07\d{3} \d{3} \d{3})$ but note that 07\d{3} gives 5 digits? 07 is 2 digits, plus 3 digits = 5 digits, then space, then 3 digits, space, then 3 digits. So total digits: 2+3+3+3=11. So that works. But the description says 'after the first five digits' meaning after the 5th digit, which is after 07XXX. So that is correct. So the regex: /^(07\d{9}|07\d{3} \d{3} \d{3})$/

description: The input must be a United States date in month/day/year order. The month and day may each be one or two digits, with no leading zero required. The year must be four digits. All three parts must be separated by the same character: either all forward slashes or all hyphens. Mixing separators is invalid.
Validate a SHA-256 digest in hexadecimal form. The digest must be exactly 64 hexadecimal characters (0-9, a-f, A-F). Only format is checked, not the actual hash.
A hexadecimal string must consist only of characters 0-9, a-f, A-F, and its length must be an even number of at least 2 characters. No spaces or other separators are allowed.

Spec: Validate a UUID string of version 4 (random). The format is 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits. The version digit (first character of the third group) must be '4'. The variant digit (first character of the fourth group) must be one of 8, 9, a, A, b, or B. Hexadecimal digits may be uppercase or lowercase. No braces or other characters are allowed.
A CSS hexadecimal color value. It starts with a hash and is followed by either exactly three or exactly six hexadecimal digits, using letters a through f in either case.
A simplified full IPv6 address: eight groups of one to four hexadecimal digits, each group separated by a colon. Groups are written in full (no :: compression). Each digit must be 0-9, a-f, or A-F.
A TCP/UDP port number as a decimal integer between 1 and 65535 inclusive. No leading plus sign, no whitespace, and no leading zeros.
A dotted-quad IPv4 address. Each of the four octets is a decimal number from 0 to 255, written without leading zeros.

intent: username with length and character rules
description:
Username rules:
- Length between 3 and 20 characters inclusive.
- Allowed characters: letters, digits, underscores and hyphens.
- Must begin and end with a letter or a digit.
- Two consecutive underscores or hyphens are not allowed anywhere.
- Underscore and hyphen must not be adjacent to each other.
twitter-style handle: @ followed by 3-15 letters digits or underscores

The contact page needs a field for a French landline number only. It must start with 0 followed by 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5, then eight further digits. The field should accept the number with optional spaces or dots between digits.

intent: IBAN format of a given country
description: Match a German IBAN: exactly two uppercase letters 'DE' followed by 20 digits. No separators or spaces are allowed. Only the format is checked, not the checksum.

A SIRET number consists of exactly 14 digits. A SIREN number consists of exactly 9 digits. The string may optionally contain spaces every 3 digits from the right, but no other separators are allowed. For SIRET, spaces are optional but if present must follow the pattern: 3 digits, space, 3 digits, space, 3 digits, space, 5 digits. For SIREN, spaces are optional but if present must follow the pattern: 3 digits, space, 3 digits, space, 3 digits.

Validate that a string is an absolute Unix path. It must start with a forward slash, followed by one or more path segments. Each segment must consist of one or more characters that are not forward slashes. Consecutive slashes are not allowed. The path must not end with a slash unless the path is exactly the root directory '/'. The root directory itself is valid.
file name without forbidden characters (no / \ : * ? " < > | and no null or control chars, must not be empty or start with a space)

Semantic version, no leading zeroes in numeric identifiers. Major, minor, patch are non-negative integers without leading zeroes. Pre-release optional: dot-separated identifiers where numeric identifiers have no leading zeroes; identifiers contain only ASCII alphanumerics and hyphens. Build metadata optional: dot-separated identifiers containing only ASCII alphanumerics and hyphens. Do not validate calendar facts or checksums.

intent: semantic version with pre-release and build metadata
description: A semantic version number in the form major.minor.patch where each part is digits without leading zeros. It may optionally have a prerelease part starting with a hyphen, made of dot-separated identifiers of letters, digits and hyphens; numeric identifiers in the prerelease must not have leading zeros. It may also optionally have build metadata starting with a plus sign, made of dot-separated identifiers of letters, digits and hyphens. Prerelease comes before build metadata if both are present.

We need to validate the version field in our release manifest. It should be a semantic version: major, minor, and patch numbers separated by dots, each number a non-negative integer without leading zeros. Don't worry about pre-release tags or build metadata—just the core version.

Match a semantic version number. It must be three dot-separated numbers—major, minor, and patch—where each number is a non-negative integer without a leading zero. Pre-release identifiers and build metadata are not allowed.

intent: log line starting with a given level
description: Log lines are accepted only when they begin with a severity level at the very start of the line. The permitted levels are DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR and FATAL, in upper case. The level must be followed by a single space. After the level, there may be any content, including content that is empty, but the level itself must not be part of a longer word, so a line such as INFOrmation is not valid.

description: The editor stores passages wrapped in quotation marks. A submission is valid when the entire string starts with a double quote or a single quote, ends with exactly the same kind of quote, and the content in between holds no quote characters of that same kind at all.

intent: number using any Unicode decimal digits
description: Match an unsigned integer consisting of one or more decimal digits from any script, such as Arabic-Indic, Devanagari or fullwidth digits.

description:

- At least one character.
- Only Greek letters are allowed (uppercase or lowercase).
- Combining marks used for Greek diacritics are allowed after a letter, but the string may not start with one.
- No spaces, digits, punctuation or characters from any other script.

Validate that a text field contains no control characters. A control character is any Unicode character in the C0 range (U+0000–U+001F) or the C1 range (U+007F–U+009F), including tab, newline and carriage return. The field may be empty and may otherwise contain any characters, including other Unicode whitespace such as a non-breaking space.

The two names must match exactly; the string is invalid if the closing name differs from the opening name.
base64 string

description: A comma-separated list of one or more integers, with no spaces around the commas and no trailing comma. Each integer is an optional minus sign followed by one or more digits; leading zeros are allowed, and a lone minus sign is not a valid integer.

description: An opening and closing tag pair with the same name, where the tag name is a letter or underscore followed by any number of letters, digits, or underscores. Both tags must have identical names, and no attributes or content are allowed between them.

- The identifier must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
- The entire string must not be equal to any of the listed reserved words.
- Matching is case-sensitive: "If" is allowed, "if" is not.

A valid Japanese yen amount consists of an optional plus or minus sign, followed by one to nine digits. No decimal places or thousands separators are allowed. The sign is optional and, if present, must be immediately before the digits. Only ASCII digits are accepted.

intent: euro price in French format (comma decimal, space thousands, trailing €)
description: A valid price in French format consists of a number with an optional space as a thousands separator (groups of three digits), a comma as the decimal separator, and exactly two decimal places. The amount must be followed by a non-breaking space (U+00A0) and then the euro sign (€). For example, "1 234,56 €" or "123,45 €" are valid. The integer part must have at least one digit. No leading plus or minus sign is allowed.
Match a three-letter English month abbreviation in any mix of upper and lower case.
iso 8601 calendar date yyyy-mm-dd with zero padded months and days

A SHA-256 digest represented as lowercase hexadecimal characters, exactly 64 characters long.

intent: ticket reference such as JIRA keys

A version 4 UUID: lowercase hexadecimal characters in the format xxxxxxxx-xxxx-4xxx-yxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx, where the third group starts with 4 and the fourth group starts with 8, 9, a, or b.
A ULID: 26 characters total, using Crockford's Base32 alphabet (0123456789ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTVWXYZ) in uppercase.

An image file name ends with one of the following extensions, ignoring case: .jpg, .jpeg, .png, .gif, .bmp, .webp, or .tiff. Before the extension, the file name must contain at least one character and must not contain a forward slash or backslash.

cal ver yyyy.mm.dd optional with patch? actually: year.month where month 01-12 and optional .day 01-31? but that's calendar fact. Let's say: calendar version with year and month, optional day, year 4 digits, month 01-12, day 01-31, separated by dots.

kubernetes resource name dns subdomain lowercase alphanumeric dashes dots

Any integer from zero upward is valid as long as its final digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. No sign, decimal point, or thousands separator may appear.

Percentage value rules for the discount input field:
- The value is between 0 and 100 inclusive.
- At most two digits may appear after the decimal point.

- The value 100 is allowed, both as a whole number and with decimals, but no value greater than 100 is accepted.

scientific notation numbers like 1.5e-10, optional sign, mantissa may be integer or decimal

Scientific notation string specification:
- An optional leading + or - sign.
- A mantissa that is either a whole number of one or more digits, or a decimal number with one or more digits before the dot and one or more digits after it. A leading zero is allowed only when it is the sole digit before the dot.
- The letter e or E.
- An optional sign, + or -, for the exponent.
- An exponent consisting of one or more digits; leading zeros are permitted in the exponent.
- No spaces are allowed anywhere.

intent: negative amounts in accounting format with parentheses
description: A negative amount written in accounting format: it starts with an opening parenthesis, then an optional currency symbol, then one or more digits, then an optional comma thousands separator followed by exactly three digits, which may repeat, then a decimal point, then exactly two digits, then an optional space, then a closing parenthesis. No space is allowed between the opening parenthesis and the currency symbol or digits.

intent: euro price in French format (comma decimal, space thousands, trailing €)
description:
Rules for a French euro price:
- The amount is a sequence of digits.
- The thousands separator is a narrow no-break space (U+202F), used between groups of three digits, starting from the right; the first group may have one to three digits.
- The decimal separator is a comma, followed by exactly two digits.
- The amount is followed by a space and the euro sign (€).
- The euro sign must be the last character.

intent: negative amounts in accounting format with parentheses
description: A negative amount in accounting format: the amount is enclosed in parentheses. Inside the parentheses there may be an optional dollar sign immediately followed by one or more digits, then an optional decimal point and exactly two digits. No thousands separators are allowed. No space is permitted between the parentheses and the content.
A yen amount: one or more digits followed by the yen sign (¥). No decimals are allowed, and no thousands separators are allowed. The yen sign must come after the digits. No spaces anywhere.

Match a European date in day/month/year form where the day and month are one or two digits with an optional leading zero and the year is exactly four digits. Only the numeric format is checked; the day is between 1 and 31 and the month between 1 and 12.

Validate a URL slug. It must be lowercase, may contain groups of letters or digits separated by single hyphens, must not start or end with a hyphen, must not contain two consecutive hyphens, and must be between 1 and 80 characters long.
uuid v4 lowercase hex only
uuid v1 uppercase allowed

Match a CSS length value: a non-negative number (integer or decimal, optionally starting with a dot) followed immediately by one of the units px, em, rem, vh or vw. The number part must end with a digit.
Match a CSS hexadecimal color. It may be written with either three or six hex digits, and a leading hash is required. Letters may be upper or lower case.

intent: MAC address with a consistent separator
description: A MAC address consisting of exactly six two-character hexadecimal groups. All six groups must be separated by the same character, which may be a colon or a hyphen; mixing separators is invalid. Hexadecimal digits may be upper or lower case.

We need to validate the network field in the firewall configuration screen. Users enter an IPv4 network in CIDR notation: four decimal octets 0-255 separated by dots, a slash, then a prefix length from 0 to 32. Only the format is checked, not the network address itself.

Our support tool needs to accept IPv4 addresses typed into a ticket field. The address must be four decimal octets separated by dots, each octet from 0 to 255, with no leading zeros allowed (except for the single digit 0).

Validate an IPv4 CIDR block string with these rules:
1. Exactly four octets separated by dots.
2. Each octet is a decimal number from 0 to 255; leading zeros are not allowed except for the value 0 itself.
3. A single slash followed by a prefix length from 0 to 32 immediately after the fourth octet.
4. No surrounding whitespace.

Email address format (practical, not RFC-complete): local part consists of one or more allowed characters: letters (a-z, A-Z), digits, dot, underscore, percent, plus, hyphen. Consecutive dots are allowed. The local part must not start or end with a dot. Domain part: one or more labels separated by dots, each label is alphanumeric or hyphen, but must not start or end with a hyphen. The last label (TLD) must be at least two letters. Case-insensitive for domain.
French postal code. Exactly 5 digits, no spaces or separators.
A French SIRET or SIREN number. SIREN is exactly 9 digits. SIRET is exactly 14 digits. Only digits are allowed, no spaces or separators.

description: Our media library requires every uploaded asset filename to begin with an eight-digit date (YYYYMMDD) indicating the day it was added, followed by a hyphen, then a short descriptive slug. The slug must consist of lowercase letters, digits, or underscores, and must be at least one character long. No other characters or separators are allowed.

Only image files are accepted for upload. A valid filename must have exactly one dot separating the base name from the extension. The operator and version must not be separated by spaces.

description: We need to validate software version strings that follow semantic versioning, including optional pre-release labels like alpha, beta, or rc, and optional build metadata after a plus sign. Pre-release identifiers are alphanumeric with hyphens and must not be empty; build metadata identifiers are alphanumeric with hyphens and also must not be empty.

BEM class name: block, element and modifier parts joined by double underscores and double dashes, e.g. block__element--modifier. Each part is a lowercase word made of letters and digits, words may be joined by single hyphens but never start or end with one and never have two hyphens in a row. No element or modifier may be empty, but both are optional. No underscores other than the double separators.

valid js identifier, ascii only: starts with letter, $ or _, then letters digits $ _, and must not be one of the reserved words
kebab-case name: lower case letters and digits in groups separated by single hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen
environment variable name: uppercase letters, digits and underscores, cannot start with a digit, cannot contain two underscores in a row, and must not be a reserved shell name like PATH, HOME or PWD

A whole number from 1 to 100 inclusive, with no leading zeros, no plus sign, and no minus sign.
An integer between 1 and 100 inclusive. Leading zeros are not allowed, except that the number zero itself is not allowed.

Only an integer from 1 to 100 is allowed.

3. An optional prerelease suffix may follow the patch number: a hyphen followed by one or more dot-separated identifiers, where each identifier is either all digits (no leading zero unless it is exactly 0) or a non-empty sequence of letters/digits/hyphens starting with a letter or digit.

In the release dashboard the operations team records the monthly release identifier. It always looks like the year followed by a dot and the two-digit month, with the year being any four digits from 1000 to 9999 and the month being 01 through 12. Nothing else is allowed in the field.

The major, minor and patch numbers may not have leading zeros. A numeric prerelease or build identifier also may not have leading zeros. An identifier that contains a letter or hyphen may have leading zeros. No spaces are allowed anywhere and the version must end after the patch number if there is no prerelease or build, or after the build if there is one. Only the format is checked.

Our admin panel lets support staff look up a user by typing the variable name they see in a stack trace. We're not accepting anything exotic like Unicode escapes, and no other characters or spaces at all.

- Start with a lowercase ASCII letter.
- Followed by zero or more ASCII letters or digits.
- Must not contain underscores, hyphens, spaces, dollar signs, or any other punctuation.
- No uppercase letter may appear at the very start.

We store user-defined variable names in a config editor and must reject anything that would break the parser, but the spec says we should be permissive with names people actually use. Accept ECMAScript identifiers including the Unicode escape form: either a real Unicode letter/underscore/dollar followed by real letters, digits, underscores or dollars, or a sequence built from \uXXXX escapes. Identifiers may also start with a Unicode escape representing a letter, underscore or dollar. Reject reserved words, leading digits, and any other characters.

Actually, the official format for SIRET is 14 digits, often written as SIREN (9 digits) followed by NIC (5 digits), with spaces: '123 456 789 00012'. That's 3-3-3-5. So we'll allow that.

We need to specify: The input is either:

So the regex should accept:
- 9 digits: ^\d{9}$ or ^\d{3} \d{3} \d{3}$
- 14 digits: ^\d{14}$ or ^\d{3} \d{3} \d{3} \d{5}$

Let's formalize:

A SIREN is exactly 9 digits, optionally written as three groups of 3 digits separated by single spaces.
A SIRET is exactly 14 digits, optionally written as three groups of 3 digits followed by a group of 5 digits, all separated by single spaces.

intent: git branch name following a convention
description: We need to validate branch names that our team creates for feature work and hotfixes. A valid branch name must start with either 'feature/' or 'hotfix/', followed by a short description in lowercase kebab-case: one or more hyphen-separated words, where each word consists of lowercase letters, digits, or a single dot. Additionally, the branch name must not end with a hyphen or dot. The description part may contain slashes only if they separate words, but our convention forbids slashes in the description, so no extra slashes are allowed.

intent: PIN code of 4 to 6 digits, not all identical

intent: API key with a known prefix
description: An internal service token is a fixed-format string: the literal prefix svc_, then 16 characters that may only be lowercase hexadecimal digits (0-9 and a-f). The token is always exactly that length, with no surrounding whitespace.

intent: log line starting with a given level
description: In our log viewer we only want to highlight lines that our application's own logger produced. Our logger always writes lines in the form LEVEL: message, where LEVEL is one of FATAL, ERROR, WARN or INFO and the message is the rest of the line. We must not match lines from third-party libraries that merely mention those words somewhere in the middle, so the level has to be at the very start of the line, uppercase exactly as listed, immediately followed by a colon and a single space, and then at least one character of message text. The whole line then counts as ours.

intent: HTTP status line with a 4xx or 5xx code
description:
A string is a valid HTTP status line if and only if it consists of:
- The literal 'HTTP/'
- Exactly one digit for the major version (currently 1)
- A dot
- Exactly one digit for the minor version (currently 1)
- A single space
- A three-digit status code
- A single space
- A reason phrase that is at least one character long and cannot contain newline characters
The status code must be either a 4xx or 5xx code (400–499 or 500–599).
